props.title: Ned Kelly

sections.content: **Ned Kelly** (2003) represents a pivotal modern take on Australia's most famous bushranger, with Heath Ledger's brooding performance capturing Kelly's transformation from persecuted settler to folk hero outlaw. The film follows similar thematic territory as other historical outlaw epics like **The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford** (2007) and **Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid** (1969), examining how criminal legends are born from social injustice. Director Gregor Jordan frames the Victorian-era Australian landscape with the same rugged grandeur that defined classic westerns like **The Man from Snowy River** (1982).

sections.content: The bushranger genre forms a crucial part of Australian cinema history, with Kelly's story being filmed multiple times since 1906's **The Story of the Kelly Gang**. The 2003 version distinguishes itself through its focus on the social conditions that created Kelly, particularly the persecution of Irish settlers by British colonial authorities. This approach mirrors other colonial-era resistance films like **Michael Collins** (1996) and **The Wind That Shakes the Barley** (2006), where the line between criminal and freedom fighter becomes deliberately blurred.

Recent years have seen continued fascination with the Kelly saga, notably in **True History of the Kelly Gang** (2019), which takes a more experimental approach to the legend. These films share DNA with other outlaw biopics like **Public Enemies** (2009) and **Lawless** (2012), where historical accuracy meets mythmaking. The enduring appeal of Kelly's story reflects broader themes of resistance against authority and the creation of national identity through shared narratives. sections.content: Australian frontier cinema has evolved significantly since the Kelly films of the early 20th century. Modern entries like **The Tracker** (2002) and **Gold** (2022) examine colonial-era stories through a more critical lens, acknowledging Indigenous perspectives and the complex moral landscape of frontier society. This shift parallels similar developments in American westerns, from **Dances with Wolves** (1990) to **The Power of the Dog** (2021).
